fixture_note: Calibration audit A3. Retrospective reconstruction of a real decision taken during the v0.1 build: what should happen to an option generated by an EXPLORE operator that was not present at intake. Intake is restricted to what was knowable at the decision point. The option actually chosen is NOT marked, and no evidence describing the outcome is included.

intake.problem_statement: The divergent operator generated a third option during the governance evaluation run and that option never appeared in the convergence ranking, and we must decide how generated options should be treated.
constraints: divergent is prohibited by contract from ranking or recommending an option
convergent is prohibited by contract from generating a new option at the decide stage
stage records are sealed as each stage completes, so the option set can only grow forward

observations.statement: The generated option OPT-PILOT appears in the divergent payload and is absent from the convergence ranking.
The divergent contract declares produces_options true, yet no stage downstream of it reads that field.

options.label: Rank only the options supplied at intake
options.mechanism: Restrict convergence to the option set fixed at intake and treat any option an operator generates as commentary that does not enter scoring.
options.tradeoff: The generation operator produces output that nothing consumes.

options.label: Admit generated options into the scored set
options.mechanism: Grow the option set as the route proceeds so a newly generated candidate is challenged, forecast, scored and rejected on the record like any other.
options.tradeoff: An option introduced late has fewer stages in which to accumulate evidence, so it enters scoring structurally disadvantaged.

options.label: Report generated options in a separate unscored list
options.mechanism: Publish candidates from exploration under their own receipt field marked as proposed rather than evaluated, leaving the ranking untouched.
options.tradeoff: A reader must reconcile two lists and decide for themselves whether the unscored candidate deserved evaluation.

evidence_register.locator: governance-decision receipt: divergent payload contains OPT-PILOT; convergence ranking contains OPT-ADOPT and OPT-CONDITION only
evidence_register.claim_supported: A generated option was produced and never scored.
The contract declares that this operator produces options.

evidence_register.locator: spec/operators.yaml: divergent prohibited_behaviors includes rank_or_recommend_an_option; convergent prohibited_behaviors includes generate_a_new_option_at_the_decide_stage
evidence_register.claim_supported: Neither operator may perform the other's role, so any admission must happen in the engine between them.

evidence_register.locator: docs/opportunity-brief.md: an operator whose output nothing consumes is the reasoning-theatre failure mode this system exists to prevent
evidence_register.claim_supported: Unconsumed operator output is the stated failure mode of the whole system.

evidence_register.locator: OPT-PILOT carries no claims from any operator and therefore no evidence references
evidence_register.claim_supported: The generated option would fail the evidence threshold if it were scored.

evidence_register.locator: spec/routing-policy.yaml: stage_order places EXPLORE before CHALLENGE, FORECAST and DECIDE
evidence_register.claim_supported: An option generated at EXPLORE still has every downstream stage available to it.

assumptions: The purpose of the exploration stage is to widen the option space rather than to annotate an existing one.

primitives.statement: The divergent contract declares that this operator produces options.
No stage downstream of exploration reads the generated option field.
Exploration runs before challenge, forecast and decide, so a generated option has every later stage available to it.
Neither the generating operator nor the deciding operator may perform the other's role.
Whether a late-entering option can attract enough evidence within the remaining stages is not established.

claims.statement: An operator contractually declared to produce options whose output no stage reads is performing work that cannot affect any outcome, which is the condition the system was built to detect.
Because exploration precedes every scoring stage, admitting a generated option costs no ordering violation and requires no operator to exceed its contract.

assumptions: Downstream consumers read the ranking rather than individual operator payloads.

relations.mechanism: generation proposes candidates into the set
later stages bind claims to members of the set
bound claims are aggregated into the ranking
a ranking that never contains generated candidates removes any reason to generate them

feedback_loops.effect: The return path from the ranking is what gives generation its purpose. Cut it and the loop runs open: the operator keeps producing candidates that cannot reach the ranking, so its cost is paid and none of its value is collected.

claims.statement: Excluding generated candidates from the ranking opens the only loop that gives the exploration stage its function, so the defect is structural rather than a missing feature.

assumptions: The option set must remain a deterministic function of the run.

options.label: Rank only the options supplied at intake
options.mechanism: Restrict convergence to the option set fixed at intake and treat any option an operator generates as commentary that does not enter scoring.
options.tradeoff: The generation operator produces output that nothing consumes.

options.label: Admit generated options into the scored set
options.mechanism: Grow the option set as the route proceeds so a newly generated candidate is challenged, forecast, scored and rejected on the record like any other.
options.tradeoff: An option introduced late has fewer stages in which to accumulate evidence, so it enters scoring structurally disadvantaged.

options.label: Report generated options in a separate unscored list
options.mechanism: Publish candidates from exploration under their own receipt field marked as proposed rather than evaluated, leaving the ranking untouched.
options.tradeoff: A reader must reconcile two lists and decide for themselves whether the unscored candidate deserved evaluation.

options.label: Require a human to promote a generated candidate before it is scored
options.mechanism: Hold newly proposed candidates in a pending state and admit one to scoring only after a named reviewer promotes it, recording who did so.
options.tradeoff: Introduces a human step inside a single run, so a route can no longer complete without waiting.

claims.statement: Four dispositions exist for a candidate that appears mid-run: ignore it, score it, publish it unscored, or gate it behind a named promotion.

assumptions: The omission was not deliberate policy.

hypotheses.statement: Convergence was written against the intake option list because that is where options first appear, and the generated field was never wired in, so the contract declares a capability the engine does not implement.
hypotheses.discriminating_test: Search the engine for any read of the divergent options field outside contract validation. If none exists, the capability was never implemented rather than deliberately withheld.

hypotheses.statement: Generated options were deliberately excluded to keep the option set fixed for the duration of a run, so that the set the challenge stages saw is the set the ranking scores.
hypotheses.discriminating_test: Look for a policy statement or comment declaring the option set immutable after intake. Its absence disconfirms deliberate exclusion.

claims.statement: The leading explanation is an unimplemented declared capability rather than a deliberate design constraint, and it is separable by searching for any consumer of the generated field.

defects.statement: Keeping the current behaviour requires the position that exploration exists to inform a reader rather than to widen the decision, and no document in this run states that.
defects.remediation: Either state that position explicitly in the divergent contract and set produces_options false, or admit the options.

defects.statement: The observed generated option carried no claims at all, so this run contains no case of a generated option that would have survived scoring. The benefit is asserted on a case where it changes nothing.
defects.remediation: Construct a run in which a generated option attracts supporting claims and confirm it can actually win.

defects.statement: Requiring a human promotion inside a run introduces a blocking human step into a pipeline whose determinism depends on completing without external input.
defects.remediation: Model promotion as a superseding run rather than a mid-run pause.

defects.statement: Saying admission costs no ordering violation is true of the stage sequence but silent on evidence parity, which primitive P5 records as unknown.
defects.remediation: Record whether a late-entering option can reach the evidence threshold, and if it structurally cannot, say so in the receipt.

claims.statement: Admitting generated options is argued from a case in which the generated option had no evidence and could not have won, so the mechanism is untested where it would matter.
Publishing an unscored parallel list moves the reconciliation work onto the reader, which is the outcome the ranking exists to avoid.

failure_modes.statement: The exploration operator continues to run on every route, consuming its share of the route budget, while nothing it produces can influence any recommendation.
failure_modes.precondition: The generated field remains unread and no contract check flags the inconsistency.
failure_modes.detection_signal: Generated option identifiers never appear in any ranking across a corpus of runs.

failure_modes.statement: A generated option enters scoring with no evidence, is ranked last, and its permanent presence at the bottom of every ranking trains readers to skip the tail of the list.
failure_modes.precondition: Generated options are routinely produced without any operator later binding evidence to them.
failure_modes.detection_signal: Generated options occupy the lowest rank in a large majority of runs.

failure_modes.statement: The unscored list is never read, and a genuinely better candidate sits in it unevaluated while a worse one is recommended from the ranking.
failure_modes.precondition: Readers treat the ranking as the complete option space.
failure_modes.detection_signal: A later superseding run recommends an option that appeared in an earlier run's unscored list.

failure_modes.statement: A run stalls indefinitely waiting for a promotion decision nobody has been assigned to make, and no receipt is issued at all.
failure_modes.precondition: No owner is designated for promotion and no timeout exists.
failure_modes.detection_signal: Runs in a pending-promotion state with no disposition after their expected completion window.

claims.statement: The failure mode of the current behaviour is silent and permanent, because nothing in the run reports that a produced option was discarded.
Admission fails loudly rather than silently: an evidence-starved generated option is visibly ranked last with its unmet thresholds stated, which is a reviewable outcome rather than an invisible one.

assumptions: The receipt format will be consumed by at least one other system.

effects.statement: Once one operator is known to produce output nothing consumes, the argument that operators are contract-enforced weakens generally, because the contract declared a capability the engine did not honour.
effects.follows_from: The generated option field remains unread.
effects.affected_party: anyone relying on the contract claim

effects.statement: Admitting generated options makes option provenance a field in the receipt, which lets a later reader distinguish a candidate the requester framed from one the analysis surfaced, and that distinction is itself a coverage signal.
effects.follows_from: The option set records where each candidate came from.
effects.affected_party: receipt consumers and the Leverage Engine

effects.statement: A parallel unscored list establishes that the receipt has two tiers of candidate, so later fields will be added to whichever tier is cheaper rather than whichever is correct.
effects.follows_from: Generated candidates are published outside the ranking.

claims.statement: Admission produces a durable second-order benefit the other dispositions do not: option provenance becomes visible, which turns the exploration stage into a measurable coverage signal rather than a narrative one.
